CALL TO ORDER

Meeting called to order at 3:05 PM by Co-Chair Jamies Shufford.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Tan, Topolewski, Washington, Diles III, Brezenoff, McFadzen, Richert,
Martins, Amick, Chotiswatdi, Bambrick, Boyce, McCullom, Shuford, Wee

Also present: Stephanie Sosa, Community Program Specialist, Jennifer Santana, Secretary,
Paul Duncan, Attendee, Jeffrey Proctor, Attendee.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  24-55115  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Continuum of Care (CoC) Board
  Meeting of July 09, 2024.

  A motion was made by Member Martins, seconded by Member Brezenoff, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Topolewski, Diles III, Brezenoff, McFadzen, Richert, Martins, Amick,
  Boyce, McCullom, Shuford, Wee
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Tan, Washington, Chotiswatdi, Bambrick

2.  24-54829  Recommendation to discuss and vote on CoC Board Applicants.

  • The board received two applications: Conor Lock, Deputy Mayor of Housing
  for the City of Long Beach, and Rose Buenaventura, Vice President of
  DevOps for Orange County United Way.

  Page 1 of 5
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 10, 2024
  200 W BROADWAY, LONG BEACH, CA 90802
  BILLIE JEAN KING LIBRARY, 3:00 PM

  • Applicant Rose provided a summary of her current role and interest in being
  part of the board.
  • The board voted to have both applicants on the CoC board.
  • No public comment.

  A motion was made by Co-Chair Wee, seconded by Co-Chair Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Topolewski, Diles III, Brezenoff, McFadzen, Richert, Martins, Amick,
  Boyce, McCullom, Shuford, Wee
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Tan, Washington, Chotiswatdi, Bambrick

3.  24-54830  Recommendation to receive and file the 2024-2025 CoC NOFO Overview.

  • Jeffrey Proctor from the Health Department provided an overview. HUD
  released the NOFO on August 1, 2024, and this application covers a two-
  year period.
  • The RFP release date is scheduled for the end of August, and panelists will
  assist in the review process once the RFPs are submitted.
  • HUD has identified policy priorities related to the NOFO.
  • The Long Beach CoC has renewed its status as a Unified Funding Agency.
  • Both the Long Beach CoC and HUD have prioritized permanent housing
  projects over other types.
  • The scoring categories and ranking for the NOFO were discussed.
  • The cost of living will be adjusted post-award, which is a change from HUD's
  previous practices.
  • City staff and board members engaged in conversation regarding the
  information presented.
  • No public comment

  A motion was made by Member Amick, seconded by Member Topolewski, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Topolewski, Diles III, Brezenoff, McFadzen, Richert, Martins, Amick,
  Boyce, McCullom, Shuford, Wee
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Tan, Washington, Chotiswatdi, Bambrick

4.  24-54831  Recommendation to approve the 2024 Reallocation Policy.

  • City staff member Jeffrey Proctor from the Health Department presented an
  overview of the 2024 Reallocation Policy and the language revisions that
  were implemented.
  • Members of the committee expressed concerns around accountability issues
  between the city and the funding agencies.
  • No further comments, no public comment.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Boyce, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Topolewski, Diles III, Brezenoff, McFadzen, Richert, Martins, Amick,
  Boyce, McCullom, Shuford, Wee
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Tan, Washington, Chotiswatdi, Bambrick

5.  24-54832  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff and
  Operations Update presentation by Paul Duncan from the Health Department.

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided an overview on staff promotions,
  and ongoing recruitment for various positions was discussed.
  • Three grant applications have been submitted in the month of June; ERF 3
  project is focused on the LA Riverbed.
  • $1 billion was added to HHAP round 6 for the FY 25 budget.
  • On July 12th the partnership with Project Street Vet and Kismet Pets
  launched a pet food pantry.
  • The annual overdose awareness day was hosted at the MSC on August
  29th.
  • The MSC is working on updating the kids’ corner to help make families feel
  more comfortable.
  • Board members and staff engage in conversation around the pet food
  collaboration.
  • No public comment.

  A motion was made by Member Martins, seconded by Member Boyce, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Diles III, Brezenoff, Richert, Martins, Amick, Boyce, McCullom,
  Shuford, Wee
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None

6.  24-54833  Recommendation to discuss the Memorandum dated August 12, 2024, titled City
  Response to Grants Pass V. Johnson Decision.

  • Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, presented on the city
  memo. On June 28th, 2024, the supreme court reversed the U.S. 9TH Circuit
  Court of Appeals decision in the case of Jonson V. Grants.
  • The memo provides a summary of this ruling, the additional enforcement
  capacity will be implemented, and how it will be incorporated into the City of
  Long Beach’s current homelessness response.
  • Committee members and staff had conversations around the Memo and the
  cities response, they discussed engagement around those experiencing
  homelessness and long-term goals.
  • No further comment or public comment.

  A motion was made by Member Brezenoff, seconded by Member Martins, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Diles III, Brezenoff, Richert, Martins, Amick, Boyce, McCullom,
  Shuford, Wee
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 6 Tan, Topolewski, Washington, McFadzen, Chotiswatdi, Bambrick

7.  24-54834  Recommendation to receive and file the HSAC Representative Report.

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided an overview of the last HSAC
  meeting and announced that Pam Chotiswatdi will be stepping down as the
  CoC representative. The committee will vote on a new representative at the
  next committee meeting.
  • No public comment.

  A motion was made by Member Amick, seconded by Member Richert, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:
